Analytics for a Better World, Lecture 1
This course is very hands-on… how and on what?
The book by Hillier and Lieberman uses Microsoft Excel for simple computations and Lindo for optimization models. However, Lindo is no longer widely used.
Instead, we will use Python for all computations.
Python is the preferred language throughout the Business Analytics program and is the de facto standard for most professionals in data science and analytics.
Analytics for a Better World, Lecture 1
Why python? Let's ask the world…
Analytics for a Better World, Lecture 1
According to simplilearn.com, Python is the best language to learn, regardless of your profession and interests.
The TIOBE Index consistently ranks Python as the number one programming language.
TechRadar reports that about three quarters of all developers use Python and intend to continue doing so.
The Kaggle community, strong in analytics, predominantly uses Python, as shown on the right.
Python is also a tool used by AI assistants
Analytics for a Better World, Lecture 1
The concept of a notebook is powerful: it combines formatted text, code, and results in one place. Here is an example of a notebook!
Jupyter notebooks natively support Python but can run over 40 languages.
Many distributions exist, but we will not recommend any specific one.
If you install Python and Jupyter locally, you are responsible for maintaining and troubleshooting your setup.
We will not provide technical support for personal installations.
Analytics for a Better World, Lecture 1

This is a blessing that we gladly use in our course: each notebook runs on a virtual machine deployed by Google for it, for free.
Means that it runs without installation on your machine regardless of the machine type!
